141	d4d_complex_proxy_rubric:
142	  schema_version: "2.0"
143	  description: >
144	    Ten-element hierarchical rubric for evaluating D4D YAML completeness and usability.
145	    Each element represents a complex metadata-driven goal and includes up to five measurable
146	    sub-elements. Scores can be computed at the element or sub-element level.
147	
148	  scoring_scale:
149	    element: 0–5
150	    sub_element: [0, 1]  # 0 = not present/fail, 1 = present/pass
151	
152	  rubric:
153	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
154	    - id: 1
155	      name: "Dataset Discovery and Identification"
156	      description: "Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?"
157	      sub_elements:
158	        - name: "Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)"
159	          field: ["doi", "rrid", "id"]
160	        - name: "Dataset Title and Description Completeness"
161	          field: ["title", "description"]
162	        - name: "Keywords or Tags for Searchability"
163	          field: ["keywords"]
164	        - name: "Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)"
165	          field: ["page", "resources"]
166	        - name: "Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)"
167	          field: ["parent_datasets", "related_datasets"]
168	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
169	
170	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
171	    - id: 2
172	      name: "Dataset Access and Retrieval"
173	      description: "Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?"
174	      sub_elements:
175	        - name: "Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined"
176	          field: ["license_and_use_terms", "ip_restrictions"]
177	        - name: "Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification"
178	          field: ["regulatory_restrictions", "confidentiality_level", "hipaa_compliant", "other_compliance", "governance_committee_contact"]
179	        - name: "Download URL or Platform Link Available"
180	          field: ["download_url"]
181	        - name: "Distribution Formats and File Types Specified"
182	          field: ["distribution_formats", "format", "media_type"]
183	        - name: "Related Datasets and External Resources Linked"
184	          field: ["related_datasets", "external_resources"]
185	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
186	
187	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
188	    - id: 3
189	      name: "Data Reuse and Interoperability"
190	      description: >
191	        Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?
192	
193	        Note: Evaluate whether the dataset is designed for integration with similar datasets,
194	        including: common identifiers for cross-dataset linking, standardized formats for data
195	        harmonization, and documented integration procedures.
196	      sub_elements:
197	        - name: "License Terms Allow Reuse"
198	          field: ["license_and_use_terms"]
199	        - name: "Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)"
200	          field: ["format", "encoding"]
201	        - name: "Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated"
202	          field: ["conforms_to", "conforms_to_schema"]
203	        - name: "Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined"
204	          field: ["variables"]
205	        - name: "Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)"
206	          field: ["intended_uses", "prohibited_uses", "discouraged_uses"]
207	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
208	
209	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
210	    - id: 4
211	      name: "Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards"
212	      description: "Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?"
213	      sub_elements:
214	        - name: "IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact"
215	          field: ["ethical_reviews", "human_subject_research", "data_protection_impacts"]
216	        - name: "Deidentification Method Described"
217	          field: ["is_deidentified"]
218	        - name: "Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment"
219	          field: ["participant_privacy", "reidentification_risk"]
220	        - name: "Informed Consent Obtained from Participants"
221	          field: ["informed_consent"]
222	        - name: "Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented"
223	          field: ["vulnerable_populations", "participant_compensation"]
224	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
225	
226	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
227	    - id: 5
228	      name: "Data Composition and Structure"
229	      description: "Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?"
230	      sub_elements:
231	        - name: "Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described"
232	          field: ["subpopulations"]
233	        - name: "Number of Instances or Samples Reported"
234	          field: ["instances"]
235	        - name: "Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits"
236	          field: ["variables", "is_tabular", "is_data_split", "is_subpopulation"]
237	        - name: "Data Topics or Conditions Represented"
238	          field: ["instances"]
239	        - name: "Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented"
240	          field: ["anomalies", "sampling_strategies", "missing_data_documentation"]
241	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
242	
243	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
244	    - id: 6
245	      name: "Data Provenance and Version Tracking"
246	      description: "Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?"
247	      sub_elements:
248	        - name: "Dataset Version Number Provided"
249	          field: ["version"]
250	        - name: "Version Access Methods Documented"
251	          field: ["version_access"]
252	        - name: "Change Descriptions and Errata Provided"
253	          field: ["errata", "updates"]
254	        - name: "Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated"
255	          field: ["updates"]
256	        - name: "Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources"
257	          field: ["was_derived_from", "release_notes", "raw_data_sources"]
258	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
259	
260	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
261	    - id: 7
262	      name: "Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency"
263	      description: "Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?"
264	      sub_elements:
265	        - name: "Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation"
266	          field: ["purposes"]
267	        - name: "Primary Research Objectives or Tasks"
268	          field: ["tasks"]
269	        - name: "Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed"
270	          field: ["funders"]
271	        - name: "Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present"
272	          field: ["funders"]
273	        - name: "Creators and Acknowledgements Documented"
274	          field: ["creators", "funders"]
275	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
276	
277	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
278	    - id: 8
279	      name: "Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)"
280	      description: >
281	        Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?
282	
283	        Note: Preprocessing and collection metadata may be represented as structured text
284	        descriptions OR as machine-readable provenance graphs (e.g., W3C PROV-O, workflow graphs).
285	        Evaluation should check for: (1) structured text descriptions OR (2) graph representations
286	        with entity-activity-agent relationships. Both formats are acceptable.
287	      sub_elements:
288	        - name: "Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described"
289	          field: ["collection_mechanisms"]
290	        - name: "Data Acquisition Methods Listed"
291	          field: ["acquisition_methods"]
292	        - name: "Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality"
293	          field: ["preprocessing_strategies", "cleaning_strategies", "labeling_strategies", "annotation_analyses", "machine_annotation_tools"]
294	        - name: "Software and Tools Documented"
295	          field: ["software_and_tools"]
296	        - name: "External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols"
297	          field: ["external_resources", "conforms_to", "imputation_protocols"]
298	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
299	
300	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
301	    - id: 9
302	      name: "Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure"
303	      description: "Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?"
304	      sub_elements:
305	        - name: "Known Limitations Documented"
306	          field: ["known_limitations"]
307	        - name: "Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)"
308	          field: ["known_biases"]
309	        - name: "Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted"
310	          field: ["anomalies"]
311	        - name: "Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided"
312	          field: ["sensitive_elements", "content_warnings"]
313	        - name: "Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis"
314	          field: ["ethical_reviews", "future_use_impacts"]
315	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
316	
317	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
318	    - id: 10
319	      name: "Cross-Platform and Community Integration"
320	      description: >
321	        Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?
322	
323	        Note: For Bridge2AI datasets, citation metadata is mandatory and should include:
324	        (1) formatted citation string, (2) DOI, and (3) citation instructions. Hosting
325	        platform identification should specify the publisher or repository (e.g., PhysioNet,
326	        Dataverse, institutional repositories).
327	      sub_elements:
328	        - name: "Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform"
329	          field: ["publisher"]
330	        - name: "Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing"
331	          field: ["citation", "doi"]
332	        - name: "Community Standards or Schema Conformance"
333	          field: ["conforms_to"]
334	        - name: "Outreach Materials and Documentation Links"
335	          field: ["external_resources", "page"]
336	        - name: "Related Datasets with Typed Relationships"
337	          field: ["related_datasets"]
338	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

        - name: "Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined"
          field: ["variables"]
        - name: "Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)"
          field: ["intended_uses", "prohibited_uses", "discouraged_uses"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 4

      sub_elements:

    - id: 6
      name: "Data Provenance and Version Tracking"
      description: "Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Dataset Version Number Provided"
          field: ["version"]
        - name: "Version Access Methods Documented"
          field: ["version_access"]
        - name: "Change Descriptions and Errata Provided"
          field: ["errata", "updates"]
        - name: "Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated"

        - name: "Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources"
          field: ["was_derived_from", "release_notes", "raw_data_sources"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    - id: 7
      name: "Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency"
      description: "Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation"
          field: ["purposes"]
        - name: "Primary Research Objectives or Tasks"
          field: ["tasks"]
        - name: "Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed"
          field: ["funders"]
        - name: "Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present"
          field: ["funders"]
        - name: "Creators and Acknowledgements Documented"

        - name: "Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described"

        - name: "Data Acquisition Methods Listed"
          field: ["acquisition_methods"]
        - name: "Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Validate D4D evaluation JSON files against their schemas.

This ensures evaluations conform to the standardized schema, which in turn
ensures HTML renderers can reliably parse the output.
"""
import argparse
import json
import re as _re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

try:
    import jsonschema
    from jsonschema import validate, ValidationError
except ImportError:
    print("ERROR: jsonschema package not installed")
    print("Install with: pip install jsonschema")
    sys.exit(1)


def load_schema(schema_path: Path) -> Dict:
    """Load JSON Schema file."""
    with open(schema_path, 'r') as f:
        return json.load(f)


def load_evaluation(eval_path: Path) -> Dict:
    """Load evaluation JSON file."""
    with open(eval_path, 'r') as f:
        return json.load(f)


#: Top-level keys of the shape that preceded the current agent contract.
#: rubric10 evaluations recorded before 2026 report `summary_scores` and
#: `element_scores`; the agents have instructed `overall_score` and `elements`
#: since. Such a record is not wrong, it is a different vintage — reporting it
#: as invalid buries the records that really are.
SUPERSEDED_SHAPE_KEYS = ("summary_scores", "element_scores")


def classify(eval_data: Dict, schema: Dict) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
    """Validate, distinguishing a superseded shape from a wrong value.

    Returns `("valid" | "superseded" | "invalid", errors)`.

    The distinction is the point. All 28 recorded evaluations failed before the
    schemas were brought up to the agents (#323), and "Invalid: 28" said nothing
    about which were merely old. Of the 20 that still fail, 12 predate the
    contract and 8 report `max_points: 84` — a maximum the rubric has never had
    (#314). Only the second kind is a defect in a record.
    """
    errors = []
    try:
        validate(instance=eval_data, schema=schema)
        return "valid", []
    except ValidationError as e:
        errors.append(f"Validation error: {e.message}")
        errors.append(f"  Path: {' -> '.join(str(p) for p in e.path)}")
        if e.schema_path:
            errors.append(f"  Schema path: {' -> '.join(str(p) for p in e.schema_path)}")
        if any(k in eval_data for k in SUPERSEDED_SHAPE_KEYS):
            return "superseded", errors
        return "invalid", errors


def validate_evaluation(eval_data: Dict, schema: Dict) -> Tuple[bool, List[str]]:
    """Back-compatible wrapper: superseded records are not valid."""
    status, errors = classify(eval_data, schema)
    return status == "valid", errors


def validate_outputs(paths: List[Path], rubric: str | None = None,
                     schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:
    """Require each explicitly named new output to pass its semantic schema.

    Directory names and superseded shapes do not exempt a new output. This
    path reads only the files named by the caller, so an evaluator can check
    its own output without reading another evaluator's judgements (#833).
    """
    schema_dir = schema_dir or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src/download/prompts"
    names = {"rubric10-semantic": "rubric10_semantic_schema.json",
             "rubric20-semantic": "rubric20_semantic_schema.json"}
    failed = not paths
    for path in paths:
        try:
            doc = load_evaluation(path)
            if not isinstance(doc, dict):
                raise ValueError("evaluation must be a JSON object")
            declared = doc.get("rubric")
            if not isinstance(declared, str) or declared not in names:
                raise ValueError(f"no semantic evaluation schema for rubric {declared!r}")
            if rubric is not None and declared != rubric:
                raise ValueError(f"expected {rubric}, found {declared}")
            valid, errors = validate_evaluation(doc, load_schema(schema_dir / names[declared]))
            if not valid:
                raise ValueError("\n".join(errors))
        except (OSError, ValueError, jsonschema.SchemaError) as exc:
            print(f"INVALID {path}: {exc}")
            failed = True
        else:
            print(f"VALID {path}: {declared}")
    return int(failed)


#: A directory whose name marks its contents as kept evidence rather than a
#: live artifact: an archive, a superseded set, or a dated snapshot of one
#: arm's scores. An invalid record in one of these is what an older
#: instrument produced and must not be rewritten to satisfy today's schema,
#: so it is reported and does not fail the run.
KEPT_DIR = _re.compile(r"^(?:_archive|superseded)|^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(?:[_-]|$)")


def is_kept(path: Path, base: Path) -> bool:
    """Is any directory between `base` and `path` an archive marker?"""
    return any(KEPT_DIR.match(part) for part in path.relative_to(base).parts[:-1])


def discover(base: Path) -> List[Path]:
    """Every evaluation JSON under `base`, at any depth.

    The loop was `{rubric}_semantic/concatenated/*.json` — one directory per
    rubric, one level deep (#833). That reached 28 of the 204 semantic
    artifacts on disk: not `label_aware/`, which is where every evaluation
    since 2026-08 lives and which the cross-arm table reads, not the dated
    per-arm subdirectories beside it, and not the archives. The rubric a file
    declares decides which schema it is judged against, so the directory does
    not have to.
    """
    return sorted(base.rglob("*_evaluation.json"))


def main(eval_base: Path | None = None, schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:
    """Validate every evaluation JSON under `data/evaluation_llm`.

    The two roots are arguments so that the exit code — the thing #833 asked
    for, and the thing four tests of the helpers did not reach — can be
    exercised end to end over a tree built for the purpose.
    """
    base_dir = Path(__file__).parent.parent
    schema_dir = schema_dir or base_dir / "src" / "download" / "prompts"
    eval_base = eval_base or base_dir / "data" / "evaluation_llm"

    schemas = {
        "rubric10-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric10_semantic_schema.json"),
        "rubric20-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric20_semantic_schema.json"),
    }

    eval_files = discover(eval_base)
    if not eval_files:
        print(f"No evaluation files found in {eval_base}")
        return 1

    print(f"Found {len(eval_files)} evaluation file(s) under {eval_base}\n")

    counts = {("live", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
    counts.update({("kept", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")})
    no_schema: Dict[str, int] = {}
    live_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []
    kept_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []

    for eval_file in eval_files:
        where = "kept" if is_kept(eval_file, eval_base) else "live"
        shown = eval_file.relative_to(eval_base)
        try:
            eval_data = load_evaluation(eval_file)
            if not isinstance(eval_data, dict):
                raise ValueError("evaluation must be a JSON object")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"❌ {shown}: failed to load: {e}")
            counts[(where, "unreadable")] += 1
            continue

        rubric = eval_data.get("rubric", "unknown")
        if rubric not in schemas:
            # Named and counted, not skipped in silence: the presence-style
            # rubric10/rubric20 outputs have no schema in this repository, and
            # a reader of the summary should see that they were not judged.
            no_schema[str(rubric)] = no_schema.get(str(rubric), 0) + 1
            continue

        status, errors = classify(eval_data, schemas[rubric])
        counts[(where, status)] += 1
        if status == "invalid":
            (kept_invalid if where == "kept" else live_invalid).append((shown, errors))
        elif status == "superseded":
            print(f"🕐 {shown}: superseded shape — {errors[0]}")

    for label, rows in (("live", live_invalid), ("kept as evidence", kept_invalid)):
        for shown, errors in rows:
            print(f"❌ {shown} ({label}):")
            for error in errors:
                print(f"     {error}")

    print()
    print("=" * 60)
    print("SUMMARY (judged against a schema):")
    for where in ("live", "kept"):
        row = {k: counts[(where, k)] for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
        print(f"  {where:5}  valid {row['valid']:4}  superseded {row['superseded']:3}  "
              f"invalid {row['invalid']:3}  unreadable {row['unreadable']:3}")
    if no_schema:
        print("  no schema in this repository, not judged: "
              + ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in sorted(no_schema.items())))
    print("=" * 60)

    # A superseded record is historical output of a contract that no longer
    # applies, and one kept under an archive marker is evidence of what an
    # older instrument produced: reported, never rewritten to pass. Only a
    # live invalid artifact fails the run.
    return 0 if not live_invalid and not counts[("live", "unreadable")] else 1


def cli(argv: List[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--file", type=Path, action="append", dest="files",
                        help="validate this exact new output strictly; repeat for multiple files")
    parser.add_argument("--rubric", choices=("rubric10-semantic", "rubric20-semantic"),
                        help="require the named outputs to use this rubric")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.rubric and not args.files:
        parser.error("--rubric requires --file")
    return validate_outputs(args.files, args.rubric) if args.files else main()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(cli())

171	purposes:
172	- response: >-
173	    To enable future generations of artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) research to
174	    provide critical insights into type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), including salutogenic pathways
175	    to return to health.
176	- response: >-
177	    To collect and publicly share a multimodal, AI-ready dataset for studying the pathogenesis and
178	    salutogenesis of T2DM, uniformly balanced for T2DM severity across a diverse group of
179	    participants recruited at three geographically distinct sites.
180	- response: >-
181	    To develop a foundational dataset in T2DM, agnostic to existing classification criteria or
182	    biases, that can be used to reconstruct a temporal atlas of T2DM development and reversal
183	    towards health.
184	- response: >-
185	    To create a model for developing large scalable datasets, sharing a blueprint that future data
186	    generation projects can follow for collecting and sharing AI-ready datasets.

188	addressing_gaps:
189	- response: >-
190	    The ability to understand and affect the course of complex, multi-organ diseases such as T2DM
191	    has been limited by a lack of well-designed, high quality, large, and inclusive multimodal
192	    datasets.
193	- response: >-
194	    A major barrier has been the lack of diverse datasets that are AI ready for training AI models;
195	    the AI-READI dataset is intended to fill this gap.
196	- response: >-
197	    Existing large datasets for AI/ML training have inherent limitations of demographic imbalance;
198	    a meta-epidemiological review of T2DM studies published from 2000 to 2020 found that samples
199	    lacked racial and ethnic diversity, and this collection is an important step forward in
200	    addressing those demographic inequities in research.

587	    demographic information, the Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression Scale (CES-D-10),
588	    Problem Areas in Diabetes (PAID-5), a diabetes self-care score, a dietary assessment, an
589	    ophthalmic/visual impairment and eye care survey, smoking, alcohol, vaping and marijuana use
590	    history (marijuana not assessed in Alabama), a general health history, PhenX social
591	    determinants of health surveys, and a current medications log with RxNorm codes.
592	- mechanism_details: >-
593	    12-lead electrocardiography with the Philips PageWriter TC30 Cardiograph, performed with the
594	    participant reclining or supine and the chair position recorded.
595	- mechanism_details: >-
596	    Blood pressure and heart rate measured twice with automatic oscillometric devices: OMRON HEM
597	    907XL, Medline MDS4001 Automatic Digital Blood Pressure Monitor, or Welch Allyn 6000 series
598	    vital signs monitor with a FlexiPort reusable cuff.
599	- mechanism_details: >-
600	    10 g monofilament testing of touch perception at three locations on each foot for peripheral
601	    neuropathy, with results recorded on an iPad, laptop or paper questionnaire and entered into
602	    REDCap.
603	- mechanism_details: >-
604	    Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) administered electronically on an iPad using the MoCA Duo
605	    application, capturing the total score, section subscores, Memory Index Score and task
606	    completion times.
607	- mechanism_details: >-
608	    Visual acuity measured with the M&S Technologies Electronic Visual Acuity (EVA) tester at 4
609	    meters under photopic conditions and under mesopic conditions using a 2.0 neutral density
610	    filter, each eye separately and best corrected.
611	- mechanism_details: >-
612	    Letter contrast sensitivity measured with the MARS Letter Contrast Sensitivity test
613	    (Perceptrix) monocularly under photopic and mesopic (neutral density occluder) conditions.
614	- mechanism_details: >-
615	    Autorefraction with the Topcon KR 800 auto keratometer/refractor, and lensometry with the NIDEK
616	    LM-600P, Topcon CL-200 or Topcon CL-300 lensometers.
617	- mechanism_details: >-
618	    Undilated handheld color fundus photography with the Optomed Aurora IQ, a non-mydriatic
619	    handheld camera with a 50 degree field of view and 5 Mpix sensor.
620	- mechanism_details: >-
621	    Dilated widefield TrueColor confocal fundus imaging with the iCare EIDON, in fully automated
622	    mode, capturing single-field central infrared and fundus autofluorescence images and a smart
623	    horizontal mosaic.
624	- mechanism_details: >-
625	    Optical coherence tomography and OCT angiography with the Heidelberg Spectralis HRA+OCT using
626	    the ONH-RC, PPole-H and macular OCTA protocols.
627	- mechanism_details: >-
628	    Fluorescence lifetime imaging ophthalmoscopy with the Heidelberg FLIO, macula-centered, acquired
629	    last in the visit.
630	- mechanism_details: >-
631	    Swept-source OCT and OCTA with the Topcon DRI OCT Triton, using 12.0 x 12.0 mm and 6.0 x 6.0 mm
632	    OCTA and 12.0 x 9.0 x 6.0 mm 3D horizontal and radial scan modes.
633	- mechanism_details: >-
634	    OCT, OCTA and color fundus photography with the Topcon Maestro2 3D OCT-1 robotic system, using
635	    12.0 x 9.0 mm widefield, 6.0 x 6.0 mm 3D macula and 6.0 x 6.0 mm OCTA (50 kHz) protocols.
636	- mechanism_details: >-
637	    OCT and OCTA with the Zeiss Cirrus 5000 Angioplex, using 512 x 512 and 200 x 200 macula and
638	    optic nerve head scans and macular OCTA.
639	- mechanism_details: >-
640	    Dexcom G6 real-time integrated continuous glucose monitoring system, worn continuously for 10
641	    days after the visit, capturing readings every five minutes; participants were masked to the
642	    results during the monitoring period.
643	- mechanism_details: >-
644	    Garmin Vivosmart 5 fitness activity tracker, worn for 10 consecutive days on the participant's
645	    chosen wrist, with the wrist worn and the dominant hand recorded on a returned data sheet;
646	    sampling frequency 5 seconds.
647	- mechanism_details: >-
648	    LeeLab Anura, an environmental sensor unit custom designed for the AI-READI project at the
649	    Karalis Johnson Retina Center, University of Washington, placed in a frequently used area of
650	    the participant's home for 10 days; the placement location was recorded on return.
651	- mechanism_details: >-
652	    Non-fasting blood and urine collection during the visit, with complete blood counts run by
653	    Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments-certified laboratories local to each data collection
654	    site and all other assays performed by the University of Washington Nutrition and Obesity
655	    Research Center testing facility on stored frozen samples.

693	direct_collection:
694	- is_direct: true
695	  collection_details: >-
696	    The data was collected directly from participants across the three recruiting sites; this was
697	    active data collection rather than passive collection or secondary use of existing data.
698	    Recruitment pools were identified by screening electronic health records for diabetes and
699	    prediabetes ICD-10 codes among patients with an encounter in the sites' health systems.

701	sampling_strategies:
702	- is_sample: false
703	  is_random: false
704	  is_representative: false
705	  strategies: >-
706	    Non-probability sampling. A contact pool was identified for each recruitment wave by screening
707	    electronic health records at each site using ICD-10 codes (R73.09 for pre-diabetes and E11.X
708	    for T2DM) and demographic data; invitations were mailed and emailed with personalized links
709	    into an online REDCap recruitment interface. Recruitment proceeded in waves whose composition
710	    and size were influenced by the observed participation characteristics of race/ethnicity,
711	    gender, severity of T2DM and site, with under- and oversampling of groups as needed.
712	  source_data: >-
713	    All patients aged 40 years or older who had a medical encounter within each health system site
714	    (University of Alabama at Birmingham, University of California San Diego, University of
715	    Washington).
716	  why_not_representative: >-
717	    Rather than targeting the demographic distribution of the US population, the study is
718	    triple-balanced by recruiting four race/ethnic groups (Asian, black, white, Hispanic), four
719	    categories of T2DM severity and biological males and females in equal proportions, because
720	    building balanced datasets is critical for the development of unbiased machine learning models.

748	cleaning_strategies:
749	- cleaning_details: >-
750	    Quality control measures were applied at the time of data entry and acquisition: clinical data
751	    outside expected minimum/maximum ranges were flagged in REDCap and surfaced in reports viewed
752	    by clinical research coordinators and data managers, who examined participant records to
753	    determine whether an error was likely. Data were checked, and edited where errors were
754	    detected, for credibility against prespecified reasonable ranges, incorrect flow through
755	    prescribed skip patterns, missing data that could be filled directly from other portions of an
756	    individual's record, and the omission or duplication of records. Editing was done only under
757	    the guidance and approval of the site principal investigator; where there was no logical or
758	    appropriate way to correct a value, the site PI decided whether it should be removed.

760	preprocessing_strategies:
761	- preprocessing_details: >-
762	    After data were sent from the study sites to the central project team, all data were mapped to
763	    standardized terminologies where possible, including the Observational Medical Outcomes
764	    Partnership (OMOP) Common Data Model for clinical data and DICOM for medical imaging;
765	    proprietary device exports were transformed into standard model formats before upload to
766	    FAIRhub, with Topcon .fda and FLIO .sdt files converted to DICOM and Garmin .FIT files
767	    converted to the Open mHealth standard. Processing for this release combined automated and
768	    custom steps, in contrast with the custom/ad hoc processing of version 1.0.0.

770	    No instances were excluded at the time of preprocessing; exclusions arise only from the study
771	    eligibility criteria (age 40 or older, able to consent, able to read and speak English, not
772	    pregnant, no gestational diabetes, no type 1 diabetes).

name: Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project
title: Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project
description: >-
  The AI-READI flagship dataset is a multimodal, AI-ready dataset of type 2 diabetes mellitus
  (T2DM) collected from individuals with and without T2DM and harmonized across three data
  collection sites (University of Alabama at Birmingham, University of California San Diego, and
  University of Washington). Version 3.0.0 contains data from 2280 participants collected between
  July 19, 2023 and May 1, 2025; it comprises 356,343 files and is around 3.82 TB in size.
  Modalities include survey and clinical data mapped to the OMOP Common Data Model, blood and urine
  laboratory results, physical measurements and vision testing, cognitive (MoCA) and monofilament
  testing, 12-lead electrocardiography, retinal photography, optical coherence tomography (OCT),
  OCT angiography (OCTA), fluorescence lifetime imaging ophthalmoscopy (FLIO), continuous glucose
  monitoring, wearable activity monitoring, and home environmental sensor data; these encompass
  tabular data, imaging data and physiological signal/waveform data, and no unstructured text.
  Recruitment sampling aimed at an approximately equal distribution of participants across diabetes
  severity, sex and race/ethnicity so that the collection would support downstream AI/ML analyses
  of salutogenesis, the pathway from disease to health, in T2DM. Study visits lasted a single
  session of roughly 2.5-4 hours followed by 10 days of at-home monitoring. The released data
  contain no protected health information; information related to the sex and race/ethnicity of
  participants and to medications used has been removed from this public release.

  The release is organized following the Clinical Dataset Structure (CDS) v0.1.1, with one

  Data files follow the WaveForm DataBase (WFDB) format for electrocardiography, the Observational

  Communications in Medicine (DICOM) for retinal FLIO, OCT, OCTA and photography, Open mHealth for
  wearable activity and continuous glucose monitoring data, and the NASA ASCII File Format

  packaged as an RO-Crate whose ro-crate-metadata.json conforms to RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT and the

notes: >-
  Both FAIRhub dataset pages and the AI-READI documentation site carry the notice "This repository
  is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives."
source_caveats: >-
  Institutional attribution differs across sources. The FAIRhub metadata and the license name
  Washington University in St. Louis (ROR 01yc7t268) as managing organization, lead sponsor and
  Licensor, while NIH RePORTER records award OT2OD032644 to the University of Washington, and the
  healthsheet, the BMJ Open protocol and the IRB protocol place the reviewing IRB at the University
  of Washington; the RO-Crate labels the IRB "Washington University IRB" yet gives the University
  of Washington Human Subjects Division address and the hsdrely@uw.edu contact. Both tier-1
  statements are reported rather than reconciled. License naming also differs between two tier-1
  sources: the FAIRhub API records "AI-READI custom license v2.0" (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036)
  while the FAIRhub dataset page labels the license "Health Data License"; the API value was used.
  total_file_count and total_size_bytes are the values FAIRhub states; this record's own sum of the
  nine data-type directory file counts is 356,334 (4,515 + 7 + 2,232 + 7,969 + 56,478 + 173,721 +
  93,921 + 15,245 + 2,246), nine fewer than the stated 356,343, and the structure description lists
  exactly nine root-level metadata files; the same sum over directory sizes is 3,815,969,360,064
  bytes, 419,614 bytes less than the stated 3,815,969,779,678. Collection start is 2023-07-19 in
  the FAIRhub metadata and healthsheet, while the BMJ Open protocol states enrollment began on 18
  July 2023. FAIRhub records a de-identification type of "NoDeIdentification" (no identifiers were
  collected) while the RO-Crate records the release as deidentified and the Nature Metabolism
  comment describes HIPAA Safe Harbor stripping of the public set; all three statements are carried
  in is_deidentified. Variable-level detail is drawn from the BMJ Open protocol publication and the
  healthsheet device descriptions rather than from the released data dictionary; the authoritative
  per-domain variable documentation at docs.aireadi.org was not part of the input bundle. One
  healthsheet answer states the dataset "contains data from all participants who have been enrolled
  during the first year of data collection", which is inconsistent with the same document's
  statement that this version covers July 19, 2023 to May 1, 2025.

purposes:
- response: >-
    To enable future generations of artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) research to
    provide critical insights into type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), including salutogenic pathways
    to return to health.
- response: >-
    To collect and publicly share a multimodal, AI-ready dataset for studying the pathogenesis and
    salutogenesis of T2DM, uniformly balanced for T2DM severity across a diverse group of
    participants recruited at three geographically distinct sites.
- response: >-
    To develop a foundational dataset in T2DM, agnostic to existing classification criteria or
    biases, that can be used to reconstruct a temporal atlas of T2DM development and reversal
    towards health.
- response: >-
    To create a model for developing large scalable datasets, sharing a blueprint that future data
    generation projects can follow for collecting and sharing AI-ready datasets.

addressing_gaps:
- response: >-
    The ability to understand and affect the course of complex, multi-organ diseases such as T2DM
    has been limited by a lack of well-designed, high quality, large, and inclusive multimodal
    datasets.
- response: >-
    A major barrier has been the lack of diverse datasets that are AI ready for training AI models;
    the AI-READI dataset is intended to fill this gap.
- response: >-
    Existing large datasets for AI/ML training have inherent limitations of demographic imbalance;
    a meta-epidemiological review of T2DM studies published from 2000 to 2020 found that samples
    lacked racial and ethnic diversity, and this collection is an important step forward in
    addressing those demographic inequities in research.

tasks:
- response: >-
    Downstream pseudo-time manifold analysis, an approach used to predict disease trajectories by
    collecting and learning from complex, multimodal data from participants with differing disease
    severity (normal to insulin-dependent T2DM).
- response: >-
    Development of AI/ML models of salutogenesis in type 2 diabetes, and of multimodal models over
    survey, clinical, imaging, waveform, wearable and environmental data.

other_tasks:
- task_details: >-
    The dataset is hypothesis agnostic and carries no labels, so it is intended to facilitate
    multiple potential downstream AI/ML applications beyond those the creators planned; researchers
    may define their own tasks and labels, for which the project provides no formal guidelines.

intended_uses:
- use_category: Type 2 diabetes research
  usage_notes: >-
    Access requires agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research; FAIRhub
    records the dataset consent as permitting the public version to be used only for type 2
    diabetes related research, with a private version allowing more generic use.
- use_category: Research and commercial artificial intelligence and machine learning development
  usage_notes: >-
    The license grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to download, reproduce and use the
    data and to create derivative works for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes; it
    was specifically tailored to enable reuse for commercial or research purposes while imposing
    strong requirements around data usage, security and secondary sharing to protect participants.
  examples:
  - >-
    Licensees may make, reproduce and distribute models, algorithms and programs developed, trained
    or adapted using the data, provided those models do not themselves contain the data.

prohibited_uses:
- prohibition_reason: >-
    Making clinical treatment decisions based on the data is not permitted; the data are intended
    solely as a research resource.
- prohibition_reason: >-
    Using or attempting to use the data, alone or with other information, to compromise the
    confidentiality or privacy of a data subject, to identify or contact any data subject or group
    of data subjects, to extract or extrapolate identifying information, to establish a data
    subject's membership in a particular group, or otherwise to cause harm or injury to a data
    subject is not permitted, in order to protect study participants under the license agreement.
- prohibition_reason: >-
    Sharing or distributing the data with any third-party model vendor or developer for training or
    development purposes, including model weight modification or other adjustment of a model's
    logic or operation, is not permitted even where the vendor is party to a HIPAA Business
    Associate Agreement with the licensee's institution; this prevents memorization or
    reconstruction of participant data by third-party models. Only short-term interaction such as
    prompting or querying by a BAA-covered model vendor is allowed.
- prohibition_reason: >-
    Transferring, licensing, sublicensing, selling, assigning, displaying, sharing or otherwise
    conveying any portion of the data or any derivative work to a third party that is not itself a
    licensee bound by an identical agreement is not permitted; this is the secondary-sharing
    control required to protect study participants.
- prohibition_reason: >-
    Reproducing data in papers, articles, presentations, analyses, reports or publications beyond
    small representative samples in up to five images or figures per paper is not permitted, and
    larger amounts of data shall not be published, posted or otherwise made available via
    supplemental files, zip archives, code packages or other means.
- prohibition_reason: >-
    Removing, obscuring, altering or masking the static watermarking that may be applied to
    identify the licensee is not permitted; the watermarking is a security measure supporting
    traceability of released copies.

future_use_impacts:
- impact_details: >-
    The creators do not currently anticipate uses of the dataset that could result in unfair
    treatment of individuals or groups or other harms, but note a theoretical risk of future
    re-identification. AI algorithms can infer individual patient characteristics and could
    facilitate individual-level identification, which the project addresses with a data
    dissemination system, a strict license agreement and data watermarking for both the public and
    the controlled sets.

instances:
- instance_type: Individual study participant
  counts: 2280
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:43
  label: false
  label_description: >-
    No labels or targets are provided. No specific labeling was performed, as the dataset is a
    hypothesis-agnostic dataset aimed at facilitating multiple potential downstream AI/ML
    applications; no annotation software or annotator information applies.
  notes: >-
    Each instance consists of all of the data available for an individual participating in the
    study, across survey, clinical, retinal imaging, environmental sensor, continuous glucose
    monitor and wearable activity monitor modalities.
  missing_information:
  - missing:
    - Data for one or more modalities for some participants
    why_missing:
    - >-
      Some participants elected not to participate in some study elements; in a few cases the data
      collection device had no stored results or was returned too late to retrieve them (for
      example the battery died and data was lost); in a few cases a data collision occurred at some
      point in the process and data was lost.
  - missing:
    - Participant sex, race, ethnicity and medications used
    why_missing:
    - >-
      Removed from this public release; the release documentation states that these variables,
      together with 5-digit zip code, genetic sequencing data, past health records and traffic and
      accident reports, are not included in the public dataset.

missing_data_documentation:
- missing_data_patterns: >-
    Not all modalities are available for all participants; within survey data, skipped questions
    and incomplete responses occur. Sex, race, ethnicity and medications used are absent for every
    participant in this release, having been removed before publication.
  missing_data_causes: >-
    Some participants elected not to participate in some study elements. In a few cases the data
    collection device did not have any stored results or was returned too late to retrieve the
    results, for example because the battery died and data was lost. In a few cases there may have
    been a data collision at some point in the process and data has been lost. Wearable data are
    additionally affected by improper use and by technical failure such as battery failure or
    system malfunction, and the Garmin Vivosmart 5 had to be recharged every 2-3 days, leaving gaps.
    Imaging data are affected by patient uncooperation, image noise, system malfunction and data
    transfer failures, and manually operated devices sometimes led to a modality being skipped.
  handling_strategy: >-
    Missing data that could be directly filled from other portions of an individual's record were
    filled during data cleaning under the guidance and approval of the site principal investigator;
    where there was no logical or appropriate way to correct a value, the site principal
    investigator decided whether the value should be removed. No imputation of missing modality
    data is described, and no instances were excluded at the time of preprocessing.

relationships:
- relationship_details: >-
    All instances are part of the same prospective data generation project (AI-READI), and there is
    currently only one visit per participant. Within the release, every data type, modality and
    device directory contains one folder per participant named with the participant's study ID, so
    a participant's records can be linked across modalities.

subpopulations:
- name: Self-reported race and ethnicity
  subpopulation_elements_present: false
  identification: >-
    Self-reported race/ethnicity was used to balance recruitment but is not released as a
    participant-level variable in the public version of the dataset; the healthsheet answers "No"
    to whether the dataset identifies demographic sub-populations.
  distribution: >-
    Although the variable is not released per participant, the release summary table reports
    aggregate counts across the 2280 participants of 380 Hispanic, 545 Asian, 519 Black and 836
    White participants.
- name: Biological sex
  subpopulation_elements_present: false
  identification: >-
    Biological sex was used to balance recruitment and the recommended splits but is not released
    as a participant-level variable in the public version of the dataset.
  distribution: >-
    Although the variable is not released per participant, the release summary table reports
    aggregate counts of 951 male and 1329 female participants across the 2280 participants.
- name: Diabetes status group
  subpopulation_elements_present: true
  identification: >-
    Participants were recruited into four study groups: no type 1 or type 2 diabetes; pre-type 2
    diabetes or type 2 diabetes controlled by lifestyle adjustments; type 2 diabetes controlled by
    oral or non-insulin injectable medications; and insulin-controlled type 2 diabetes.
  distribution: >-
    776 participants with no diabetes, 560 lifestyle-controlled, 686 controlled by oral or
    non-insulin injectable medication and 258 insulin-controlled.
- name: Age
  subpopulation_elements_present: true
  identification: >-
    Eligibility required an age of 40 years or older, with a protocol maximum of 85 years.
  distribution: Mean age 60.8 ± 11.3 years across the 2280 participants.

splits:
- split_details: >-
    The release includes a recommended split into training (1576 participants), validation (352)
    and test (352) sets, assigned per participant in participants.tsv. Because sex, race and
    ethnicity are not released with the public version, the project team prepared splits in
    70%/15%/15% proportions in which the validation and test sets are balanced as well as possible
    for sex, race/ethnicity and diabetes status (no diabetes, prediabetes/lifestyle controlled,
    oral medication controlled, and insulin controlled). Mean age is 61.1 ± 11.3 years in the
    training set, 60.3 ± 10.8 in validation and 60.5 ± 11.4 in test. The recommended split is new
    in version 3.0.0 and is intended to reduce disparities in models developed using this dataset.

anomalies:
- anomaly_details: >-
    In survey data, skipped questions or incomplete responses are expected.
- anomaly_details: >-
    In wearable data, improper use and technical failure such as battery failure or system
    malfunction are expected. The Garmin Vivosmart 5 had to be charged every 2-3 days, so there are
    gaps in activity data collection.
- anomaly_details: >-
    In imaging data, patient uncooperation, noise that may obscure the images, technical failure
    such as system malfunction, and data transfer failures are expected.
- anomaly_details: >-
    Undilated handheld fundus photography with the Optomed Aurora is challenging because the pupil
    is not dilated and the camera is handheld, so image quality varies from patient to patient and
    within the same patient.
- anomaly_details: >-
    FLIO acquisition takes longer than a standard Spectralis OCT and exposes participants to
    uncomfortable levels of light, so it is performed last in the visit and participants may not be
    at their best possible compliance; the device cannot tolerate more than one centimeter of
    movement during acquisition.
- anomaly_details: >-
    Devices operated manually rather than automatically (for example the Heidelberg Spectralis) can
    raise quality issues that led to skipping a modality and missing data.

known_biases:
- bias_type: selection_bias
  bias_description: >-
    Participants are volunteers, so there is selection bias known as volunteer bias which may limit
    the generalizability of the results among those who are not represented in the study
    population.
- bias_type: representation_bias
  bias_description: >-
    While the cross-sectional database ultimately aims to achieve balance across race/ethnicity,
    biological sex, and diabetes presence and severity, the pilot phase is not balanced across
    these parameters, and enrollment is ongoing so periodic releases may not have achieved balanced
    distribution across groups. The cohort does not include other races/ethnicities such as Pacific
    Islanders and Native Americans.
  mitigation_strategy: >-
    Triple-balanced recruitment targets for race/ethnicity, diabetes severity and biological sex,
    with under- and oversampling of groups as recruitment progresses; three geographically distinct
    recording sites recruiting individuals from all demographic backgrounds; recommended
    training/validation/test splits balanced for sex, race/ethnicity and diabetes status.
- bias_type: sampling_bias
  bias_description: >-
    Recruitment is predominantly urban and hospital-based, drawn from patients with an encounter in
    each site's health system, which may not fully capture all possible cultural and socioeconomic
    backgrounds.
  mitigation_strategy: >-
    Uniform data collection protocols were implemented for all subjects irrespective of their
    race/ethnicity, biological sex, or diabetes severity, across all study sites, and the selection
    of study sites was intended to ensure varied representation and minimize the potential for
    sampling bias.
- bias_type: selection_bias
  bias_description: >-
    Requiring that eligible participants speak, read and understand English may have created
    challenges in recruiting Hispanic and/or Asian persons; non-English-speaking participants were
    not initially enrolled because translating all study materials was not feasible.

known_limitations:
- limitation_type: representativeness_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    The study cohort may not provide a comprehensive representation of the population: recruitment
    is predominantly urban and hospital-based and the cohort does not include races/ethnicities
    such as Pacific Islanders and Native Americans.
  scope_impact: >-
    Models derived from the dataset may not generalize to populations, settings or cultural and
    socioeconomic backgrounds that the three recruiting health systems do not reach.
- limitation_type: coverage_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Not all modalities are available for all participants, because some participants declined some
    study elements and some device data were lost or unretrievable.
- limitation_type: scope_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    This public release excludes sensitive personal health data: 5-digit zip code, sex, race,
    ethnicity, genetic sequencing data, past health records, medications, and traffic and accident
    reports are not included, and the raw, pre-standardization data are not shared.
- limitation_type: temporal_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    The design is cross-sectional with currently one visit per participant; only about 10% of the
    cohort is planned to return for a follow-up visit in year 4 of the project, so longitudinal
    trajectories cannot be observed within this release.
- limitation_type: methodological_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Multiple imaging devices were deliberately used for one measure to represent the broad range of
    equipment in clinical settings, so device make, model and scan protocol differ across
    participants and must be accounted for; device and modality information is documented to
    support repeatability.

content_warnings:
- content_warnings_present: false
  notes: >-
    The healthsheet answers "No" to whether the dataset contains data that, if viewed directly,
    might be offensive, insulting, threatening, or might otherwise pose any safety risk such as
    psychological safety and anxiety.

confidential_elements:
- confidential_elements_present: false
  confidentiality_details: >-
    The dataset does not contain data that might be considered confidential, and no personally
    identifiable information is included in the dataset.

sensitive_elements:
- sensitive_elements_present: false
  sensitivity_details: >-
    The public dataset does not contain data considered sensitive: it carries no protected health
    information, and information related to the sex and race/ethnicity of participants and to
    medications used has been removed.

is_deidentified:
  identifiable_elements_present: false
  method: HIPAA Safe Harbor
  identifiers_removed: >-
    Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule; participant sex;
    race/ethnicity; medications used
  deidentification_details: >-
    FAIRhub records a de-identification type of "NoDeIdentification" with the explanation that no
    identifiers were collected so no active de-identification was necessary, but that the team
    checked that no identifiable data per US HIPAA were present in the data. The public set is
    stripped of Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule via the Safe
    Harbor method, as well as information related to the sex and race/ethnicity of the participants
    to prevent stigmatization of findings. The RO-Crate records the release as deidentified. The
    dataset has not undergone any formal external audit, but has been reviewed internally by
    AI-READI team members for quality checks and to ensure that no personally identifiable
    information was accidentally included.

participant_privacy:
- anonymization_method: >-
    HIPAA Safe Harbor removal of protected health information before release; participants appear
    only under study participant ID numbers used as folder names.
  privacy_techniques: >-
    Removal of sex, race/ethnicity, medications, 5-digit zip code, genetic sequencing data, past
    health records and traffic/accident reports from the public release; static watermarking of
    released data to identify the licensee; license terms prohibiting attempts to identify or
    contact data subjects; access gated by verified-ID login and license assent; during collection,
    all study data and identifiable information were kept on encrypted servers or in locked
    cabinets or rooms with restricted access at all sites.
  reidentification_risk: >-
    The healthsheet states that no uses resulting in unfair treatment or harm are currently
    anticipated but that there is a theoretical risk of future re-identification.
  data_linkage: >-
    Files for all modalities are organized by participant ID, so a participant's data can be linked
    across data types within the release.

human_subject_research:
  involves_human_subjects: true
  irb_approval:
  - >-
    Protocol STUDY00016228; initial IRB approval received on December 20, 2022, with an annual
    renewal application about the status and progress of the study due within 90 days of
    expiration. Reliance agreements were in place with the IRBs of the University of Alabama at
    Birmingham and the University of California, San Diego.
  ethics_review_board: >-

participant_compensation:
- compensation_provided: true
  compensation_amount: $200
  compensation_type: >-
    Stipend for the study visit, paid through the grant funding; reasonable parking, public transit
    or rideshare costs related to the study visit are also covered, and transportation assistance
    through rideshare services was offered to participants who endorsed barriers to transporting
    themselves to study visits.
  notes: >-
    Per the IRB protocol the stipend is provided once the final data are received and the study
    devices are returned, typically at least two weeks after the study visit, and is not prorated;
    transport costs above $25 may not be reimbursed.

acquisition_methods:
- acquisition_details: >-
    Directly observable measurements taken during the study visit and the at-home monitoring
    period, including laboratory tests, vitals, physical measurements, vision and cognitive
    testing, electrocardiography, retinal imaging, continuous glucose monitoring, wearable activity
    monitoring and home environmental sensing.
  was_directly_observed: true
- acquisition_details: >-
    Participant-reported data, principally the pre-visit and in-visit questionnaires completed in
    REDCap. Verification of data entry was performed when possible, for example by cross-
    referencing entered medications with medications that were physically brought in or
    photographed by each study participant.
  was_reported_by_subjects: true
  was_validated_verified: true

collection_mechanisms:
- mechanism_details: >-
    REDCap was used to collect patient-reported questionnaire data and clinical data from the
    visit, including the medications assessment, vitals, visual acuity, contrast sensitivity,
    monofilament test results and complete blood count results; the exact forms used for data
    collection in REDCap are published with the documentation.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Standardized questionnaires administered through REDCap, including a screening questionnaire,
    demographic information, the Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression Scale (CES-D-10),
    Problem Areas in Diabetes (PAID-5), a diabetes self-care score, a dietary assessment, an
    ophthalmic/visual impairment and eye care survey, smoking, alcohol, vaping and marijuana use
    history (marijuana not assessed in Alabama), a general health history, PhenX social
    determinants of health surveys, and a current medications log with RxNorm codes.
- mechanism_details: >-
    12-lead electrocardiography with the Philips PageWriter TC30 Cardiograph, performed with the
    participant reclining or supine and the chair position recorded.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Blood pressure and heart rate measured twice with automatic oscillometric devices: OMRON HEM
    907XL, Medline MDS4001 Automatic Digital Blood Pressure Monitor, or Welch Allyn 6000 series
    vital signs monitor with a FlexiPort reusable cuff.
- mechanism_details: >-
    10 g monofilament testing of touch perception at three locations on each foot for peripheral
    neuropathy, with results recorded on an iPad, laptop or paper questionnaire and entered into
    REDCap.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) administered electronically on an iPad using the MoCA Duo
    application, capturing the total score, section subscores, Memory Index Score and task
    completion times.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Visual acuity measured with the M&S Technologies Electronic Visual Acuity (EVA) tester at 4
    meters under photopic conditions and under mesopic conditions using a 2.0 neutral density
    filter, each eye separately and best corrected.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Letter contrast sensitivity measured with the MARS Letter Contrast Sensitivity test
    (Perceptrix) monocularly under photopic and mesopic (neutral density occluder) conditions.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Autorefraction with the Topcon KR 800 auto keratometer/refractor, and lensometry with the NIDEK
    LM-600P, Topcon CL-200 or Topcon CL-300 lensometers.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Undilated handheld color fundus photography with the Optomed Aurora IQ, a non-mydriatic
    handheld camera with a 50 degree field of view and 5 Mpix sensor.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Dilated widefield TrueColor confocal fundus imaging with the iCare EIDON, in fully automated
    mode, capturing single-field central infrared and fundus autofluorescence images and a smart
    horizontal mosaic.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Optical coherence tomography and OCT angiography with the Heidelberg Spectralis HRA+OCT using
    the ONH-RC, PPole-H and macular OCTA protocols.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Fluorescence lifetime imaging ophthalmoscopy with the Heidelberg FLIO, macula-centered, acquired
    last in the visit.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Swept-source OCT and OCTA with the Topcon DRI OCT Triton, using 12.0 x 12.0 mm and 6.0 x 6.0 mm
    OCTA and 12.0 x 9.0 x 6.0 mm 3D horizontal and radial scan modes.
- mechanism_details: >-
    OCT, OCTA and color fundus photography with the Topcon Maestro2 3D OCT-1 robotic system, using
    12.0 x 9.0 mm widefield, 6.0 x 6.0 mm 3D macula and 6.0 x 6.0 mm OCTA (50 kHz) protocols.
- mechanism_details: >-
    OCT and OCTA with the Zeiss Cirrus 5000 Angioplex, using 512 x 512 and 200 x 200 macula and
    optic nerve head scans and macular OCTA.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Dexcom G6 real-time integrated continuous glucose monitoring system, worn continuously for 10
    days after the visit, capturing readings every five minutes; participants were masked to the
    results during the monitoring period.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Garmin Vivosmart 5 fitness activity tracker, worn for 10 consecutive days on the participant's
    chosen wrist, with the wrist worn and the dominant hand recorded on a returned data sheet;
    sampling frequency 5 seconds.
- mechanism_details: >-
    LeeLab Anura, an environmental sensor unit custom designed for the AI-READI project at the
    Karalis Johnson Retina Center, University of Washington, placed in a frequently used area of
    the participant's home for 10 days; the placement location was recorded on return.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Non-fasting blood and urine collection during the visit, with complete blood counts run by
    Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments-certified laboratories local to each data collection
    site and all other assays performed by the University of Washington Nutrition and Obesity
    Research Center testing facility on stored frozen samples.

data_collectors:
- role: Clinical research coordinators and research staff
  collector_details: >-
    Research personnel at the three data sites who recruited, enrolled and collected data underwent
    training by the data manager at the University of Alabama at Birmingham and worked from a
    detailed Manual of Procedures; a certification process was required of all coordinators,
    including mandatory institutional compliance training for human subject research and successful
    administration of all protocol elements to at least three volunteer practice subjects.
- role: Site data managers
  collector_details: >-
    Data managers at each site oversaw the data collection process and were responsible for the
    quality control of all data before uploading to FAIRhub.
- role: Central project team
  collector_details: >-
    Once data were sent from each of the study sites to the central project team, additional
    processing steps were conducted in preparation for dissemination.
  notes: >-
    Effort of the team members involved in data collection was supported by NIH award OT2OD032644
    based on the percentage of effort contributed, with salaries aligned to the funding guidelines
    at each site.

collection_timeframes:
- start_date: '2023-07-19'
  end_date: '2025-05-01'
  timeframe_details: >-
    Version 3.0.0 covers data collected from July 19, 2023 to May 1, 2025, that is through the end
    of the second full year of the study. The overall project timeline spans four years, one year
    for protocol development and training and years 2-4 for subject recruitment and data
    collection; the study start date is recorded as 2023-07-19 (actual) with an anticipated
    completion date of 2027-01-01, and the overall status is "Enrolling by invitation".
  source_caveats: >-
    Sources disagree on the enrollment start date. The tier-1 FAIRhub metadata and the tier-2
    healthsheet both give July 19, 2023, while the tier-3 BMJ Open protocol publication states that
    enrollment began on 18 July 2023 and will continue until 30 November 2026. The higher-ranked
    value, 2023-07-19, was used.

direct_collection:
- is_direct: true
  collection_details: >-
    The data was collected directly from participants across the three recruiting sites; this was
    active data collection rather than passive collection or secondary use of existing data.
    Recruitment pools were identified by screening electronic health records for diabetes and
    prediabetes ICD-10 codes among patients with an encounter in the sites' health systems.

sampling_strategies:
- is_sample: false
  is_random: false
  is_representative: false
  strategies: >-
    Non-probability sampling. A contact pool was identified for each recruitment wave by screening
    electronic health records at each site using ICD-10 codes (R73.09 for pre-diabetes and E11.X
    for T2DM) and demographic data; invitations were mailed and emailed with personalized links
    into an online REDCap recruitment interface. Recruitment proceeded in waves whose composition
    and size were influenced by the observed participation characteristics of race/ethnicity,
    gender, severity of T2DM and site, with under- and oversampling of groups as needed.
  source_data: >-
    All patients aged 40 years or older who had a medical encounter within each health system site
    (University of Alabama at Birmingham, University of California San Diego, University of
    Washington).
  why_not_representative: >-
    Rather than targeting the demographic distribution of the US population, the study is
    triple-balanced by recruiting four race/ethnic groups (Asian, black, white, Hispanic), four
    categories of T2DM severity and biological males and females in equal proportions, because
    building balanced datasets is critical for the development of unbiased machine learning models.
  notes: >-
    The healthsheet states that the dataset contains all possible instances, that is data from all
    participants enrolled by the data cut-off, and answers "N/A" to the question about sampling
    strategy for a sample of a larger set; the study itself is recorded as a non-probability sample
    of the health-system population described above.

raw_data_sources:
- source_description: >-
    Electronic health records at the three recruiting sites, screened for ICD-10 diabetes and
    prediabetes diagnosis codes and demographic data to identify recruitment pools.
  source_type: Electronic health records
  access_details: Used for recruitment screening only; not released as part of the dataset.
- source_description: >-
    Device-native exports written to local storage before standardization: ECG in .xml, MoCA Duo
    application output in .csv, retinal imaging in DICOM or in vendor formats (.fda for Topcon
    Maestro2 and Triton, .sdt for FLIO) later converted to DICOM, Garmin fitness tracker data in
    .FIT later converted to the Open mHealth standard, and Dexcom CGM and environmental sensor data
    in .csv.
  raw_data_format: .xml, .csv, .fda, .sdt, .FIT, DICOM
  access_details: >-
    The raw data is saved and expected to be preserved by the AI-READI project at least for the
    duration of the project, but is not anticipated to be shared outside the project team at
    present because it has not been mapped to standardized terminologies and may accidentally
    include personal health information or personally identifiable information, for example in free
    text fields; there is a possibility that raw data may be included in future releases of the
    controlled access dataset.

cleaning_strategies:
- cleaning_details: >-
    Quality control measures were applied at the time of data entry and acquisition: clinical data
    outside expected minimum/maximum ranges were flagged in REDCap and surfaced in reports viewed
    by clinical research coordinators and data managers, who examined participant records to
    determine whether an error was likely. Data were checked, and edited where errors were
    detected, for credibility against prespecified reasonable ranges, incorrect flow through
    prescribed skip patterns, missing data that could be filled directly from other portions of an
    individual's record, and the omission or duplication of records. Editing was done only under
    the guidance and approval of the site principal investigator; where there was no logical or
    appropriate way to correct a value, the site PI decided whether it should be removed.

preprocessing_strategies:
- preprocessing_details: >-
    After data were sent from the study sites to the central project team, all data were mapped to
    standardized terminologies where possible, including the Observational Medical Outcomes
    Partnership (OMOP) Common Data Model for clinical data and DICOM for medical imaging;
    proprietary device exports were transformed into standard model formats before upload to
    FAIRhub, with Topcon .fda and FLIO .sdt files converted to DICOM and Garmin .FIT files
    converted to the Open mHealth standard. Processing for this release combined automated and
    custom steps, in contrast with the custom/ad hoc processing of version 1.0.0.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    No instances were excluded at the time of preprocessing; exclusions arise only from the study
    eligibility criteria (age 40 or older, able to consent, able to read and speak English, not
    pregnant, no gestational diabetes, no type 1 diabetes).
